paper_metadata.title: Efficient State Preparation for Quantum Amplitude Estimation

summary: The paper introduces a state‑preparation method and Spin‑Echo circuit optimization for Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE), demonstrating numerical integration on IBM Q Ourense with 2–3 qubits (8192 shots) and up to kmax=16 Grover iterations. Circuit optimization approximately halves the number of A applications and reduces CNOT counts (e.g., 49 vs. 82 CNOTs for k=16 on 2 qubits). A simulated 8‑qubit example loads a Heston stochastic volatility model for European call option pricing.

experiments.description: Numerical integration of sin^2(pi x) using QAE/MLAE on real IBM quantum hardware for 2- and 3-qubit discretizations, with left/right Riemann, midpoint, and Simpson quadrature variants and Spin-Echo circuit optimization.

algorithm.variant: Maximum Likelihood Amplitude Estimation (MLAE) applied to numerical integration

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n discretization qubits encode 2^n grid points over [0,y]; an additional qubit encodes the objective function g(x)=sin^2(pi x) via controlled Ry rotations. For the hardware experiment, y is varied and the interval [0,y] is discretized using left/right Riemann, midpoint, or Simpson rules.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate integral \int_0^y sin^2(pi x) dx via QAE by measuring the probability of the ancilla qubit in |1> (or corresponding good-state probability).

problem_instance.description: One-dimensional numerical integration of g(x)=sin^2(pi x) over [0,y] for varying y in [0,1].

dataset_specification.description: Analytic function sin^2(pi x); y varied over [0,1].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize [0,y] with 2^n equally spaced grid points; use left/right Riemann, midpoint, and Simpson quadrature rules.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MLAE estimates compared against analytic integral; mean absolute error over y reported; results aggregated over repeated hardware runs with 8192 shots per circuit.

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: readout error mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation via noisy-gate insertion (1x, 3x, 5x CNOTs) with quadratic extrapolation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Precompute rotation angles for discretized quadrature points; choose k values for MLAE.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: MLAE combines measurement outcomes across k values; error mitigation and classical extrapolation applied.

results.unit: absolute error; analytic integral is exact reference
CNOT gates (special 2-qubit optimization in Appendix D)

speedup_claims.conditions: for QAE/MLAE estimation of the integral with efficient state preparation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that the advantage is limited when circuit depth/noise or discretization error dominates; QAE error is O(1/M) while Monte Carlo is O(1/sqrt(M)).

speedup_claims.conditions: via Spin-Echo circuit optimization for repeated A and A† patterns
speedup_claims.caveats: Described as asymptotically halving the number of applications of A for larger k; actual benefit depends on compilation and hardware connectivity.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/M) estimation error for QAE/MLAE; circuit depth reduced by approximately a factor of two via Spin-Echo optimization

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large logical circuits implementing QAE with many Grover iterations M to outperform Monte Carlo; current demonstration uses only 2 physical qubits and shallow circuits
limiting_factors: No comparison of runtime vs classical Monte Carlo
State preparation overhead dominates QAE advantage

notes: num_qubits=2 corresponds to the 2-qubit numerical integration experiment (1 discretization qubit + 1 objective qubit) on IBM Q Ourense; the paper also reports a 3-qubit version, but this experiment entry captures the 2-qubit hardware run as one distinct configuration. circuit_depth not explicitly given as a single depth number; only CNOT counts and k-dependent circuit sizes are reported.
Authors discuss the quadratic speedup of QAE over Monte Carlo theoretically but do not demonstrate runtime advantage experimentally.
Hardware experiment only validates circuit construction and error scaling.

experiments.description: Simulation study of European call option pricing under the Heston stochastic volatility model using QAE-style state preparation and amplitude estimation.

algorithm.variant: QAE-style pricing of a European call option under the Heston model

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit each for nu_1 and S_1, two qubits for S_2; ancilla qubits encode transition probabilities f^nu_1, f^S_1, f^S_2 and payoff g. Good state is |1111> on the four ancillas.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[max(S_T - K, 0)] for a European call option; in the discretized example, the payoff is g(S_2)=max(S_2-K,0) normalized to [0,1] by dividing by 2.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Normalization of payoff to [0,1]; good states identified by all four ancillas being |1>.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under the Heston stochastic volatility model with two time steps (t=0,1,2).

dataset_specification.description: Parameters: K=1, delta_t=1, T=2, nu_0=1, S_0=1, kappa=1, theta=1, xi=0.5, mu=1, rho=0; discretized volatility and stock-price paths.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize the stochastic process into finite grids; derive conditional probabilities from 2D normal transition laws; exploit independence of nu_t and S_t when rho=0 to factor transition probabilities.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation of the full circuit; probability of measuring |1111> compared against marginal distribution and payoff to obtain normalized expected payoff (reported as 0.1185).

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Precompute transition probabilities for the discretized Heston model and corresponding uniformly controlled Pauli rotations.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Read out probability of |1111> and compare with marginal distribution to compute normalized expected payoff.

results.unit: normalized expected payoff / probability of measuring |1111>
probability of measuring |1111> in the four ancilla qubits
ancilla qubits used to encode transition probabilities and payoff

speedup_claims.conditions: for pricing the European call option under the discretized Heston model once the state-preparation circuit is constructed
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a simulation only; no hardware run or empirical speedup is shown. The advantage is contingent on efficient state preparation and QAE execution.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QAE provides O(1/M) estimation error for the expected payoff once the state-preparation circuit is constructed
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo simulation scales as O(1/sqrt(M))

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large‑scale QAE circuits implementing stochastic process loading and amplitude estimation with many time steps and higher resolution discretization
limiting_factors: Very small discretized example (4 state qubits)
Probability loading relies on precomputed rotation angles
Quadratic speedup insufficient to overcome state preparation overhead on NISQ hardware

notes: The paper reports a simulation of the Heston-model circuit in Qiskit and gives the 8-qubit circuit structure (4 state qubits + 4 ancillas). No explicit depth or gate counts are provided for this experiment.
The Heston model experiment only demonstrates circuit construction and probability encoding; amplitude estimation speedup is discussed theoretically.

experiments.description: Hardware experiment for the numerical integration problem using a specially optimized 2‑qubit circuit compressed to only three CNOT gates (Appendix D). The circuit unitary is classically synthesized and then executed on IBM Q Ourense.

algorithm.variant: MLAE with unitary-compressed A/Q circuit (3 CNOT implementation)
algorithm.key_details: Numerical integration of sin^2(pi x) using midpoint/left/right/Simpson quadrature; circuits transpiled to exactly three CNOT gates independent of k

key_results: Average absolute error below 2^-10 (~10^-3) using Simpson’s rule at kmax = 16
All circuits executed on IBM Q Ourense with 8192 shots and error mitigation
Demonstrates improved robustness compared to deeper circuits
